chief_complaint: wing-shaped fleshy growth from inner corner onto cornea
hpi_details: 45-year-old male farmer presents with a slowly growing, fleshy, pinkish wedge-shaped tissue extending from the nasal conjunctiva onto the nasal aspect of his right cornea. Complains of mild irritation and redness when outdoors.
ideas: thinks it might be related to pterygium
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Pterygium is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Pterygium: Lubricating drops, sunglasses, surgical excision if blocks vision, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: wing-shaped fleshy growth from inner corner onto cornea

Key HPI features: A 45-year-old male farmer has a slowly growing, fleshy, pinkish wedge-shaped tissue extending from the nasal conjunctiva onto the nasal aspect of the right cornea, with mild outdoor irritation and redness.

Objective/Exam findings: Record visual acuity in each eye, lesion size/extent and proximity to the visual axis; assess corneal involvement, induced astigmatism, inflammation, and any atypical pigmentation or rapid growth.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Pterygium.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Pinguecula without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing reduced vision, corneal involvement, rapid or atypical growth, or a lesion approaching the visual axis, which needs prompt ophthalmology assessment.
management_principles: Use preservative-free lubricating drops for irritation and UV-blocking wraparound eyewear; avoid chronic unsupervised topical vasoconstrictors or corticosteroids.
Refer to ophthalmology for reduced vision, significant induced astigmatism, progressive corneal/visual-axis encroachment, substantial symptoms, or atypical features; excision is specialist-directed.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 45M farmer presenting with an asymptomatic to mildly irritating fibrovascular conjunctival growth.
reference_soap.objective: Right eye: wedge-shaped fibrovascular proliferation extending from the nasal bulbar conjunctiva onto the nasal cornea. Document visual acuity in each eye, lesion extent/proximity to visual axis, refraction or corneal astigmatism when indicated, and assess for atypical pigmentation or rapid growth.
reference_soap.assessment: Pterygium, associated with chronic UV and wind exposure.
reference_soap.plan: Recommend UV-blocking wraparound sunglasses and lubricating drops for irritation. Refer to ophthalmology for reduced vision, significant astigmatism, progressive corneal/visual-axis encroachment, substantial symptoms, or atypical features; surgical excision is specialist-directed.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Pterygium
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Pterygium
Implement evidence-based management plan: Lubricating drops, sunglasses, surgical excision if blocks vision

teaching.one_liner: Patient with a wing-shaped fleshy growth extending from the inner corner of the eye onto the cornea.
red_flags: Reduced vision, rapid or atypical growth, marked inflammation, or extension toward the visual axis requires prompt ophthalmology assessment

must_ask.say: Do you spend a lot of time outdoors, and do you wear sunglasses?
Is the right eye affected, and has the growth caused blurred vision, glare, or trouble with daily tasks?
Does the area feel irritated or gritty?
We can use lubricating drops and sunglasses, with surgery if it threatens your vision.
